*Summary*

This test case assesses the USB and storage configurations of IGEL OS.

Especially, it focuses on dynamic client drive mapping and USB access control.



*Environment*

* Test device that has USB sockets (USB 2.0 , USB 3.0, USB c )
* Formatted USB device
* Test with  *FAT-32 / EXT-4 / NTFS*  File systems (if available)
* Another USB device that is from a different category, for instance headphones and a keyboard



*Helpful Terminal Commands*

USB devices are shown in */media* by default. This path can be used to find the name of the mount point.

If standardized Custom Partition */multimedia* is used, the following sequence can be used to test functionality:

+Copy files to mount point and confirm:+

{noformat}cp /multimedia/*.* /media/[mount point]
ls -la /media/[mount point]{noformat}

+Remove files from mount point and confirm:+

{noformat}rm -r /media/[mount point]/*.*
ls -la /media/[mount point]{noformat}



{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
The following command displays vendor and product id of a USB device: 

{{lsblk}}

+Interpretation:+

{noformat}Bus 002 Device 003: ID 1234:5678 Manufacturer_Name Product_Name{noformat}

The *ID 1234:5678* contains the *Vendor ID (1234)* and *Product ID (5678)*.
{panel}

----

*Additional Information*

The option *TC setup → Devices → Storage Devices → Options → Support for built-in floppy drives* is currently out of scope, as well as are other Storage Device types such as CD/ROM, DVD, or the like.

It is possible to fine-tune access via USB to a granular level using Device rules, for instance specific product IDs or Vendor IDs can be blocked or allowed, only specific device classes such as Audio devices can be treated individually, etc. 
Refer to [https://kb.igel.com/en/igel-os-base-system/12.4/usb-access-control-in-igel-os-12|https://kb.igel.com/en/igel-os-base-system/12.4/usb-access-control-in-igel-os-12|smart-link]  for details.

*Summary*

In this test case, the various settings for the notifications tray are approved.



*Environment*

* Chromium browser installed
* Teams app installed and logged into your account to receive messages
* Another device with Teams logged in to a different account in order to send messages



{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
The following parameters determine whether messages are shown or withheld: 



*IGEL Setup > System > Notification*:

specified severity: all | info | warning | error | none

show suppressed notification in notification panel y| n

suppress notifications with a required user action y | n

action in suppressed notification with user action: default | cancel



“do not disturb” y | n  in notifications tray


{panel}



*Helpful Terminal Commands*

 The following commands are to be executed in a user terminal:

{{igel-notify-send text -m msg -t title -l info}} sends *info* message

{{igel-notify-send text -m msg -t title -l warning}} sends *warning* message

{{igel-notify-send text -m msg -t title -l error}} sends *error* message

{{igel-notify-send text -m msg -t title -l success}} sends *success* message



Send message with *required user action:* 

{noformat}igel-notify-send text \
  -t "End User License Agreement" \
  -m "Please review the EULA summary. Click Accept to accept the full EULA or Decline to cancel." \
  -l info \
  -a '{"id":1,"label":"Accept"}' \
  -a '{"id":2,"label":"Decline"}' \
  -w{noformat}



*Additional Information*

These test steps account for the statistically most frequent combinations, but feel free to vary parameters further in free testing.

In the bug [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3033|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/APPS-3033|smart-link], the tray parameters interfered with another App, which is why it is recommended to test on a realistic working environment with apps installed. 

Teams messages are only shown in the tray if they are sent by an account that is not one’s own.

This GStreamer benchmarking script can be used to test how well media playback is working, especially after updating hardware acceleration libraries like VAAPI, NVDEC, or V4L2, or after upgrading GStreamer. It helps you test video playback performance, confirm that hardware acceleration is working properly, and make sure the system behaves as expected after those updates.

It analyzes media files, detects their container and codecs, and automatically selects a hardware decoder if available (falling back to software if needed). It then measures playback performance, including precise average FPS, late and dropped frames (QoS), and CPU/memory usage. All results are saved in detailed per-file logs and a final summary CSV report for easy comparison.

Initially, the script was created to test the performance of the new FFMPEG-based multimedia playback, by comparing the multimedia playback performance between the Fluendo-based pipeline in IGEL OS 12.7.1 and the new FFMPEG-based playback in 12.7.2.[https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11320?focusedCommentId=256242|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/browse/LX8-11320?focusedCommentId=256242|smart-link]

The following parameters determine whether messages are shown or withheld:

show suppressed notification in notification panel *y*| n

The Distributed Peer Update feature in IGEL OS 12  allows IGEL OS 12 devices to act as local update servers. Instead of each device downloading updates from the central update server, peer devices get the updates from each other. The IGEL Discovery service allows endpoint devices on the same local network to automatically find and obtain updates from one another.
*Environment*

* In large-scale tests (many devices / Proxmox-based setup --> _See:_ [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QA/pages/674464996/Large-Scale+Testing+of+Distributed+Peer+Updates+in+Proxmox|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QA/pages/674464996/Large-Scale+Testing+of+Distributed+Peer+Updates+in+Proxmox|smart-link] ), all monitoring and observation is done via the central update / discovery monitoring server logs (e.g. which device acts as fallback client, which devices are waiting, and which device downloads from which source). Network sniffing is not required in this mode.
* In small-scale tests (only a few devices), monitoring and observation is done directly on the devices, e.g. by checking the {{journalctl}} logs for the IGEL Discovery service to see which device requests, serves, or uses fallback.

The igelrmserver-port is optional, by default the 8443 is assumed.

*Summary*

_Automated device registration_

The DNS A record and the DHCP options 224+226 (structuretag) are alternative ways to tell IGEL devices where the UMS server is located. 

_Structure tag assignment_
If you configure and provide option 224 and in addition 226 (for automatically assigning the device to a certain folder in UMS devices) via DHCP-Server, IGEL endpoints will use these settings to find UMS and do not require a DNS entry named {{igelrmserver}}.
IGEL endpoints will sent a discover message/request to the DHCP server when booting and will get the IP of the UMS and also the umsstructure-tag to register on the UMS. Via the default directory rules it will be assigned to the correct device-folder 

_Autoregister using mass deployment key and ca-cert fingerprint_
As an add-on from 12.7.4 we also need to test if the device is auto-registered in a controlled way with mass deployment key and ca-cert fingerprint (UMS setting for automatic registration of any new device on the network is DISABLED).

* Check if igf239 is deleted.
* When partition check = true. Reboot.
* After reboot. Check *Cache Partition* (igf239).

The *Cache Partition* (igf239) is created automatically and the App starts without any problems.

This test case summarizes the general steps required for Horizon Certification and consolidates them into a cohesive set of instructions. For detailed and up-to-date information, always refer to the latest official Horizon certification documentation.

_Important note: Test steps may be updated. Always verify that you are using the most recent version of the Horizon documentation before execution._

Relevant Documentation Sources:

* {{Thin_Client_Certification_Guide}}
This test case includes test steps from version V2309, Chapter 6.
* {{Horizon_Cloud_Service_Next_Gen}}
This test case includes test steps from version V2306, Section 5.

h2. Additional Information:

For Horizon Certification, two main deployment scenarios must be validated. Each scenario includes specific test requirements defined by VMware Horizon:

# On-Premises Deployment
# Cloud Deployment

Both processes must be successfully validated to complete certification.

h3. Credentials:

All required credentials can be found in the password vault entry:
“Horizon Certification | On prem and cloud”

Ensure credentials are verified before starting the test execution.

h3. Documentation & Test Data:

Certification documentation and related data are provided by the Product Management (PM) team.

h3. Hardware Requirements:

The hardware used for testing is defined in the corresponding test plan. 

h3. Log Collection Requirements:

Logs must be saved locally on the IGEL OS client in the following directories:

/tmp/teradici-user/
/tmp/vmware-user/

Ensure logs are collected and preserved for validation and submission purposes.

h3. Virtual Machines:

It is not required to use all available virtual machines. In general, the following VMs are sufficient for testing:

* qa-horiz-w10-1.qa.test
* qa-horiz-w10-2.qa.test

h4. Additional Information

* Before performing the test, make sure that the Horizon Server is on the same version as the client
* If errors occur while testing, they can be traced via local terminal and the following command:

{noformat}journalctl -t Horizon -f{noformat}

* Note for PCoIP client-side image cache size setting: it cannot be fully validated in this test case as the Omnissa Horizon client does currently not expose cache utilization metrics, bandwidth impact statistics, or rendering engine behavior. Only subjective performance improvements (e.g., smoother scrolling, reduced redraw lag) and basic RAM usage can be observed. For detailed cache analytics, external network monitoring or Horizon Agent-side logging is required.
* Do *not use backslash character* (\) *within* the *password* for this test.
** Hint: If you're using an apostroph (") within your password, you must "escape" the apostroph by typing a backslash (\) in front of it
(example: for password Xy"z123 you have to type Xy/"z123).
* You will need to set *_Configure Server certificate verification mode_* to _Allow unverifiable connections_
This is a requirement based on our QA Servers

h4. Required Hardware

* Any audio speaker, microphone, USB-Stick and Composite USB Device

*How to get vid and pid of USB Device*

* run {{lsusb}} in terminal as root
>> This will yield several entries as output like the following one:

{noformat}Bus 003 Device 002: ID 047f:430f Plantronics, Inc. Poly EncorePro 310{noformat}

* The last bit informs you of which device this entry refers to
Search for the correct one that resembles the USB Device you search for
>> Plantronics Poly EncorePro 310 is our connected USB Headset for this example
* The part _047f:430f_ in this entry is the vid and pid of the device
>> vid = 047f
>> pid = 430f

*Composite USB Redirection*
_Composite USB Devices are devices that have several different features combined in one device. Eg. A keyboard with smartcard reader and speakers. Horizon allows the configuration of each component individually._
_When we redirect the composite USB device, normally the whole device is forwarded to the virtual host. However, now there is the possibility to split and forward only the child interfaces that use a generic USB channel. To do this, we need to add the following filter parameters (split and intf) to the device rules._

_Note: Make sure that “Default rule” for USB Redirection is set to “Deny” before testing this Horizon Feature._

Run lsusb to identify the vid and pid

Run lsusb -t to identify the “intf” value for configuration of the product rule

Output might look something like this

{noformat}Bus 04.Port 1: Dev 1, Class=root_hub, Driver=xhci_hcd/4p, 10000M
/:  Bus 03.Port 1: Dev 1, Class=root_hub, Driver=xhci_hcd/12p, 480M
    |__ Port 2: Dev 2, If 0, Class=Hub, Driver=hub/3p, 480M
        |__ Port 3: Dev 8, If 0, Class=Billboard, Driver=, 12M
        |__ Port 3: Dev 8, If 1, Class=Vendor Specific Class, Driver=, 12M
        |__ Port 4: Dev 18, If 2, Class=Chip/SmartCard, Driver=usbfs, 12M{noformat}

How to identify the correct Device and Feature of the Device?
In this case it is the last line. It contains the term “SmartCard” which is exactly what our connected composite USB Device has
The “If 2” is what we need as a value for intf. Add a “0” in front of this to create the value needed for the Product Rule.

This is an example of the configuration of the Product Rule with the Smartcard Feature of our connected composite USB keyboard

||*Rule*||*Vendor ID*||*Product ID*||*Extra Config*||*Name*||
|Allow|0bda|30af|split=1|intf=02|

The “split” parameter specifies whether a composite device must be forwarded as separate devices or as a single composite device. "split=1" means that the selected child interfaces of a composite device must be forwarded as split devices, while “split=0” must not be forwarded.

There are 3 possible rules:

* CONNECT = Allow redirection and connect automatically. Hotplug possible and redirection should always work
* DENY = Deny redirection of features at any time
* ALLOW = Allow redirection of feature and only connect feature if its plugged in to the device on boot. Hotplug will kill the redirection.

This Test Case covers the printing via an Windows SMB Print Server.

In this Use Case Scenario, a windows machine is set up as a print server and has all printers connected to it. On the IGEL OS devices a printer is configured, with the windows machine as server address. The print task is created by IGEL OS, pushed to the windows machine which then processes it and pushes it further to the printer.



*Additional Information*

* You may need admin rights on the windows machines in order to configure the printer. In this case reach out to colleagues, admin or your superior



*Configuring the Printer on Windows*

# Open “Printers & Scanners” in Windows
# Select the Printer and click on “Manage”
# Go to “Printer Properties”
# Go to the “Sharing” Tab. Select “Change Sharing Options”. Set “Share this printer” to _true_. Assign a “Share Name”.
# Select the “Microsoft PS Class Driver” in the “Advanced” Tab
_Note: Depending on the actual printer used for this test, you may need to select a different driver._

h2. How to get Vendor ID (VID) and Product ID (PID) of a USB Device:

Run the following command in the IGEL terminal as root:

{noformat}lsusb{noformat}

Output will look like:

{noformat}Bus 003 Device 002: ID 047f:430f Plantronics, Inc. Poly EncorePro 310{noformat}

The part {{047f:430f}} contains the *VID* and *PID*:

* *vid = 047f*
* *pid = 430f*

h2. *How to use GIMP for IADR Scanner Redirection*

* Open GIMP
* Go to File > Create > Scanner/Camera…
* Select Source
_Note: For the redirection it will only name the channel and not the device itself. This is fine_
* New Pop-Up for Scanning will come up. Start the Scan.
>> Result: Scanned document will be loaded into GIMP and can be saved

If GIMP is not installed, install it yourself or contact Admin

h2. *How to Test a Serial Port with PuTTY*

# Open *PuTTY* and select *Serial* as the connection type.
# Enter the correct *COM port number* (from Device Manager) and set the baud rate .
# Click *Open* to start the session.
# With a *loopback adapter* connected, type any text , if it echoes back, the serial port is working.

h2. *Test Serial Port via Device Manager (if PuTTY fails)*

# Open *Device Manager* → expand *Ports (COM & LPT)*.
# Check if the *COM port appears* (e.g., COM3)
# Right-click the COM port → *Properties*.
# Under *Port Settings*, adjust speed/baud rate .
# Go to the *Events* or *Resources* tab to confirm the port is working without conflicts.

h2. Test defining interface of usb devices

* This test should show that only the specified interfaces of a usb device are redirected into the remote session
* Take a usb device (e.g. Logitech webcam)
* Identify the interfaces of the video class with (e.g. Logitech C270 webcam has two video class and two audio class interfaces)
{noformat}lsusb -v -t{noformat}
* Navigate to _TC Setup > Apps > IGEL Advanced Device Redirection USB > Settings_:
** Device Rules
*** Identify the numbers of the interfaces you want to redirect (from lsusb -v -t)
*** Example output: “Port 1: Dev 2, If 0, Class=Video, Driver=uvcvideo, 480M” (here the interface is 0)
*** Enter the values in Interfaces (e.g. 0,1)
*** Connect to remote session with Fabulatech USB redirection installed on server side
*** Redirection of configured class interface works (e.g. video of webcam camera is redirected while microphone of the webcam remains in IGELOS)

h3. Acceptance Criteria:

* *Config Assumptions*:
** IGEL-discovery is available but disabled by default.
** Distributed Per Update Server is available but disabled by default.
** All devices in the same subnet use:
*** the same configuration for Distributed Per Update Serverand IGEL-discovery
*** the same port
*** the same certificates (if any) for Distributed Per Update Server
* *Criteria:*
* Roles
** Any node with IGEL-discoveryd enabled can request applications.
** Any node with IGEL-discoveryd + Distributed Per Update Server enabled can provide applications.
** A node with IGEL-discoveryd only (no Distributed Per Update Server) must never respond to requests.
* Requesting an App
** When a node requests an app, IGEL-discovery returns exactly one of these answers:
*** {{SERVER_READY + IP}}
**** The app is available.
**** The node can immediately download the app from {{IP}}.
*** {{SERVER_BUSY}}
**** The app exists in the network.
**** No node can serve it right now.
**** The requester must wait and ask again later.
***  {{FALLBACK}}
**** No node in the network has the app.
**** The requester must use the fallback mirror.
*** In case of {{FALLBACK}}, an election is started:
**** Only one node is allowed to download the app from the fallback mirror.
**** The first requester wins, based on a timestamp in the election messages.
* Providing an App
** When IGEL-discoveryd receives a request, it answers based on Distributed Per Update Server + app state:
*** {{SERVER_READY}}
**** The app is fully available locally.
**** The Distributed Per Update Server still has free connections to serve it.
*** {{SERVER_BUSY}}
**** The app is not ready to be served. This is true if:
***** The node is currently downloading the app (it is not completely present), or
***** All Distributed Per Update Server connections are already in use.
** If a node starts downloading an app via {{FALLBACK}}, that node must answer
{{SERVER_BUSY}} to all other requests for that app until its download is complete.
** As a result, when one system in the subnet starts downloading an app,
other systems must wait. After the first download is complete,
remaining devices download one after another, in a tree-like fashion.
** The IP returned by IGEL-discovery for {{SERVER_READY}} must always belong to a system
that actually hosts the requested app.
** Clients connect to exactly one server and keep that connection until
the download is complete. Other clients must respect the server’s busy/ready state.
** Fallback to multiple servers for the same app must not happen in parallel.
In a typical unsynchronized network, only a few devices should ever use fallback
for the same app at roughly the same time. Hard guarantees are not required,
but concurrent mass fallback must be avoided.
* Failure & Recovery
** If a Distributed Per Update Server goes down during a download, the client must:
*** Reinitialize the IGEL-discovery/election process,
*** Select a new server, and
*** Restart the download.
** Automatic recovery is required only when the download source is a Distributed Per Update Server.
If the download uses the fallback mirror, failures keep the old behavior
and the client shows an error instead of auto-recovering.
* Migration
** During migration via the existing static server configuration must continue to work as before.
** IGEL-discovery–based distribution is not yet required for migration to be considered successful, as long as the legacy static server path is functional.
{panel}

h3. +Additional information:+

Confluence pages for UMS as a CA → {color:#ffc400} {color}[https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EM/pages/270827521/Using+the+UMS+as+a+Certificate+Authority|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EM/pages/270827521/Using+the+UMS+as+a+Certificate+Authority|smart-link]  + [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EM/pages/455671848/Internal+How+To+Getting+Started+with+the+CA+Proxy+Feature|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/EM/pages/455671848/Internal+How+To+Getting+Started+with+the+CA+Proxy+Feature|smart-link]

Link to 30-day Lab environment creation site  →  [https://azuremarketplace.microsoft.com/de-de/marketplace/apps/certifiedsecuritysolutionsinc.keyfactor_pqc_lab?tab=Overview|https://azuremarketplace.microsoft.com/de-de/marketplace/apps/certifiedsecuritysolutionsinc.keyfactor_pqc_lab?tab=Overview|smart-link]

* Do not use your [igel.com|http://igel.com/] credentials for accessing the deployment. There will be an error due to missing permissions.
* Use your Azure credentials of one of your OBS users for that you’ve created an own EntraID in the past
** If you don’t have an extra EntraID, create on. It is free of charge.



h2. Checking for the Certificates on the Endpoint

* The successfully enrolled certificate is permanently saved in the */wfs/igel-certs* directory on the device.
* The directory is structured by the particular friendly name of a certificate: */wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME>/*…
* Each enrolled certificate is stored as a PKCS12 file (e.g. */wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME>/cert.pfx*).
** The PKCS12 file is password protected using the previously configured password. The PKCS12 contains the following entities:
*** Private Key
*** Certificate
*** Issuer CA certificates
* The entities from the PKC12 container are additionally created in the particular certificate directory:
** */wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME>/cert.pem*  - This is the enrolled certificate in PEM format
** */wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME>/pkey.pem* - Private key in PEM format protected by the configured password
** */wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME>/cacerts.pem* - The CA certificate(s)
** */wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME>/cacerts/<CN>.pem*  - The CA certificate from the bundle cacerts.pem
* The CA certificates are additionally installed into a local OpenSSL repository of CAs, so the propagated CA certificates are automatically available to all applications using OpenSSL. (symlink to */wfs/ca-certs*)
** */wfs/ca-certs/IgelCertificateAuthority.crt -> /wfs/igel-certs/<FRIENDLY NAME/cacerts/IgelCertificateAuthority.pem*
* The entire action is logged into the journal log and can be reviewed by the command:
{{journalctl | egrep 'issueclientcert|igel-certs'}}



h2. Acceptance Criteria

h4. *Initial Certificate Enrollment*

* If feature is active in UMS, the OS generates a CSR (Certificate signing request) based on the configured attributes.
* The OS transmits the CSR to the UMS securely using the configured protocol.
* Upon receiving a signed certificate, the OS stores it locally and makes it available for authentication.

h4. *Certificate Renewal*

* The OS tracks the expiration date of the installed certificate.
* When the expiration date is within the configured renewal window:
** The OS generates a new CSR.
** The OS sends the CSR to the UMS and replaces the certificate once a new one is received.

*Summary*

With the new IGEL Subscription License we need to test some specific edge/corner cases due to Workspace Licenses still being around for many customers. This Test Case covers this transition period for the forthcoming years of gradually phasing out the Workspace License with the new IGEL Subscription License.

This happens in situations like Google Maps, which require the user first to consent to use GPS data to locate the user or for Outlook to first login into the Account. *How to get vid and pid of USB Device*

* run _lsusb_ in terminal as root
>> This will yield several entries as output like the following one:

{noformat}Bus 003 Device 002: ID 047f:430f Plantronics, Inc. Poly EncorePro 310{noformat}

* The last bit informs you of which device this entry refers to
Search for the correct one that resembles the USB Device you search for
>> Plantronics Poly EncorePro 310 is our connected USB Headset for this example
* The part _047f:430f_ in this entry is the vid and pid of the device
>> vid = 047f
>> pid = 430f

*Composite USB Redirection*

_Composite USB Devices are devices that have several different features combined in one device. Eg. A keyboard with smartcard reader and speakers. Citrix allows the configuration of each component individually._
_When we redirect the composite USB device, normally the whole device is forwarded to the virtual host. However, now there is the possibility to split and forward only the child interfaces that use a generic USB channel. To do this, we need to add the following filter parameters (split and intf) to the device rules._

_Note: Make sure that “Default rule” for USB Redirection is set to “Deny” before testing this Citrix Feature._

Run lsusb to identify the vid and pid

Run lsusb -t to identify the “intf” value for configuration of the product rule

Output might look something like this

{noformat}Bus 04.Port 1: Dev 1, Class=root_hub, Driver=xhci_hcd/4p, 10000M
/:  Bus 03.Port 1: Dev 1, Class=root_hub, Driver=xhci_hcd/12p, 480M
    |__ Port 2: Dev 2, If 0, Class=Hub, Driver=hub/3p, 480M
        |__ Port 3: Dev 8, If 0, Class=Billboard, Driver=, 12M
        |__ Port 3: Dev 8, If 1, Class=Vendor Specific Class, Driver=, 12M
        |__ Port 4: Dev 18, If 2, Class=Chip/SmartCard, Driver=usbfs, 12M{noformat}

How to identify the correct Device and Feature of the Device?
In this case it is the last line. It contains the term “SmartCard” which is exactly what our connected composite USB Device has
The “If 2” is what we need as a value for intf. Add a “0” in front of this to create the value needed for the Product Rule.

This is an example of the configuration of the Product Rule with the Smartcard Feature of our connected composite USB keyboard

||*Rule*||*Vendor ID*||*Product ID*||*Extra Config*||*Name*||
|Allow|0bda|30af|split=1|intf=02|

The “split” parameter specifies whether a composite device must be forwarded as separate devices or as a single composite device. "split=1" means that the selected child interfaces of a composite device must be forwarded as split devices, while “split=0” must not be forwarded.

There are 3 possible rules:

* CONNECT = Allow redirection and connect automatically. Hotplug possible and redirection should always work
* DENY = Deny redirection of features at any time
* ALLOW = Allow redirection of feature and only connect feature if its plugged in to the device on boot. Hotplug will kill the redirection. Manual activation of redirection possible via Citrix Toolbar.

Further information on this Citrix Feature can be found here
[https://help-docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-workspace-app/windows/composite-usb-device-redirection.html|https://help-docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-workspace-app/windows/composite-usb-device-redirection.html|smart-link]

h2. *Changelog taken from App Store for new Login Handling in Citrix*

*Changes since: 2503 BUILD 1.0*
*New Features*
The IGEL login dialogue has been visually and functionally improved and requires IGEL OS 12.5 or newer. The dialogue now uses the system's own look and feel, which makes it blend in better with the overall appearance of the system. The user interface has also been optimised: The domain field, which was previously only greyed out, is now completely hidden if it is not required. During input, the first empty field is automatically focussed, which is helpful, for example, if the user name has already been pre-filled. Furthermore, the login can now be completed by pressing the enter key in any input field, which significantly speeds up the login process.
In addition, the authentication logic has been enhanced. The IGEL login dialogue now supports changing expired passwords and responds to failed authentications with appropriate feedback. Technically, the new IGEL UIDialogLib library has been introduced to provide these extended functions. The use of this new library is activated by default via a registry key:

||*Registry*||*Type*||*Value*||
|app.cwa.configuration.login.use_igel_uidialoglib|bool|true (default)/ false|

For smartcard and multifactor authentication please use the authentication method Citrix login.
Resolved Issues
Fixed password change within Citrix Workspace App with German user interface language.
Enhanced Kerberos/AD and Last User/-Domain/Autologin for Citrix Cloud Services.
Known Issues
In combination with base system below 12.6.0: The Citrix session autostart does not work as expected. As a workaround, a delay of 1 second must be set up.
Keyboard sync mode selection once/dynamic/off results in unexpected behavior.
A cryptic error message may be displayed when logging in to Citrix Cloud. Here it can help to set the parameter cwa.authman.authmanlight.longlivedtokensupport to true.

_TC Setup > Apps > Citrix > Citrix Session > Authentication = Authentication method_

*Registry Key for Login Library*
_app.cwa.configuration.login.use_igel_uidialoglib = false / true (boolean)_
Default Value is true. This Registry keys decides which library is used to handle the login dialog
True configures to use the IGEL library. False means citrix

*How to check that the correct library is used?*
_To do so, run the following command in terminal as root_

{noformat}ls -l /services/cwa/opt/Citrix/ICAClient/lib/UI*{noformat}

It will output quite a bit of text. Important is the last bit of the last line
The symlink path shown by this command is either …/*citrix*/UiDialogLibWebKit3_ext.so or …/*cuurent*/UiDialogLibWebKit3_ext.so
_The …/citrix/… part indicates that the citrix library is used_

*Use Case Information:*
*Why is it important to implement this idea? (both for customers and business)*

Allianz expects to update 20k Devices at once in a very short time frame. Improved handling of App and Profile changes is needed to ensure that updates can be done in time:

* Implemente Remote Start per real-time Clock (rtcwake is already part of OS12) and works so configuration and calling is needed.
* Implement Maintenance Window, system to check for Updates only during this time frame not directly on start and shuts down afterwards when wake-up source was real-time Clock. 
* Improved handling of profile settings in combination with app version
* profile settings are only applied if app version is activated. This prevents new settings from being applied to old not jet updated app versions.
* Reporting moved to separate ticket.

*What problems are we trying to solve? (both for customers and business)*

Currently on start of IGEL OS it will immediately start the update which leads to a massive bandwidth issue in the morning. Move Update to Off work Time for rollout of a client update chunk of up to 20k devices helps.

h2. Customer Release Notes

Rework update parameter for better control of how assigned apps should be handled. Registry keys where kept to be backward compatible.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* New update parameters
** Assign apps via UMS but do nothing on device
** Suppress download notification → only show when finished
** Nothing action when download is finished → No notification device will keep running
* Configurable local jobs
** system → customization → local jobs
* Two types of jobs
** custom
*** can run any custom command
** update
*** Download/activate apps assigned via UMS
* Jobs can be run as user or root
* Each job has some parameters
** Calendar time
*** [systemd calendar|https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.time.html#Calendar%20Events] time when to run the job
** Wake system
*** Wakeup the system from suspend and shutdown → please test on different hardware so we get some feedback if the feature is working on which hardware

How to ACME:

Automatic Certificate Management Environment Client (ACME) for IGEL OS  to deploy device certificates using ACME instead of using SCEP.

For the moment we are using the dev environment - bookworm-acme.scepandmore.test.

For questions regarding the environment please reach out to Anton Womela.

Get root-ca (CA attached below) and copy it to the desired device into /wfs/ca-certs/ - *make sure to set the permissions accordingly!* 

Go to the Registry system.network.acmeclient 

* enable the service
* enter the path for the root-ca in “cabundle”
* enter server url - [https://acme.scepandmore.test:44433/acme/acme/|https://my-stepca.example.com/acme/acme/directory]directory
* enter E-Mail address

Under /wfs/acme_certificates/default ( default when not edited in registry) a certificate should be added.

To check the content of the certificate → openssl x509 -noout -test -in client.cert -text

For the renewal of a certificate 2 prerequisites are to be fulfilled
Certificate renewal period must be set to 31 days. ACME will use the existing client certificate as a reference. This configuration means, it will renewal the client certificate x (or 31 in our case) days before expiration of the current certificate.
It will check for the expiration of an certificate in intervals configured in the configuration “Certificate expiry check interval (days)”. The GUI and the registry will only allow to configure whole numbers. Therefore we use the following command to accelerate the process:
_setparam app.acme_client.checkinterval 0.00694_ (which is roundabout 10 mins)
With _get app.acme_client.cert0.checkinterval_ we can check if the parameter before was successfully applied.
With the command _kill_postsetupd ; write_rmsettings_ we kill the already configured day and time setting of ACME and force it to run again with the newly configured interval of 10mins

* Device is managed by Daniel Willer’s UMS

How to ACME:

Automatic Certificate Management Environment Client (ACME) for IGEL OS  to deploy device certificates using ACME instead of using SCEP.

For the moment we are using the dev environment - bookworm-acme.scepandmore.test.

For questions regarding the environment please reach out to Anton Womela.

Get root-ca (CA attached below) and copy it to the desired device into /wfs/ca-certs/ - *make sure to set the permissions accordingly!*

Go to the Registry system.network.acmeclient

* enable the service
* enter the path for the root-ca in “cabundle”
* enter server url - [https://acme.scepandmore.test:44433/acme/acme/|https://my-stepca.example.com/acme/acme/directory]directory
* enter E-Mail address

Under /wfs/acme_certificates/default ( default when not edited in registry) a certificate should be added.

To check the content of the certificate → openssl x509 -noout -test -in client.cert -text

For the renewal of a certificate 2 prerequisites are to be fulfilled
Certificate renewal period must be set to 31 days. ACME will use the existing client certificate as a reference. This configuration means, it will renewal the client certificate x (or 31 in our case) days before expiration of the current certificate.
It will check for the expiration of an certificate in intervals configured in the configuration “Certificate expiry check interval (days)”. The GUI and the registry will only allow to configure whole numbers. Therefore we use the following command to accelerate the process:
_setparam app.acme_client.checkinterval 0.00694_ (which is roundabout 10 mins)
With _get app.acme_client.cert0.checkinterval_ we can check if the parameter before was successfully applied.
With the command _kill_postsetupd ; write_rmsettings_ we kill the already configured day and time setting of ACME and force it to run again with the newly configured interval of 10mins

Insights:

There was a race condition when installing both a ‘community app developer certificate’ and a community app at the same time. Ideally, RMagent would install the certificates first, then install the app but this id difficult because the UMS sends the requests independently and RMagent works on them without any specific order.

On top of that, other types of certificates, e.g. browser certificates, may have the exact opposite requirement: first install the browser app, then the certificates which are then processed by a script which adds them to a browser-specific [binary] database.

This test case covers the process of installing a community app with corresponding certificate adn to check if the order is working.

column31: VMware Horizon Broker: qa-horizon-cs.qa.test (192.168.8.175)

This tool is designed to monitor Citrix sessions contineously,  it provide detailed information about launched sessions and their resources. It sends a signal over dbus as the status changes in the citrix session, from login to logoff. Tool continiously looks for status changes, for example when the user logged in, when a resource is launched, or closed, logoff or disconnect. at every status change dbus sends a signal, you can observe it in the dbus-monitor. Currently, it monitors storefront and browser sessions only. In addition this tool also controls the running sessions using method calls. like signout and disconnect.



Also, there are wrapper scripts called sessionhandlers for logoff and disconnect (Mainly used by IAFI agent), these scripts run either without arguments or with arguments (--igelsession, or --resource), if they are executed without arguments, all running sessions are logged off/disconnected.

* *Without Arguments:*
When called without any arguments, the script attempts to apply the action to all available sessions or resources. We must verify that it correctly handles all active sessions/resources and reports a successful completion code (return_code=0).
* *With Arguments (Session Names (--igelsession) or Resource Lists (--resource)):*
When provided with specific session names, resource names, or lists of these, the script targets only those sessions or resources. We must check that the script accurately identifies matching sessions/resources, applies the requested action, and returns a structured response indicating success, partial success, no matches, or errors. The return codes specifies the actual outcome.

*Expected Behavior:*

* *Accurate Return Codes* 
** {{return_code=0}} for full success,
** {{return_code=1}} for partial success (some targets processed, others failed),
** {{return_code=2}} if no matching targets are found (no action will be done).
** {{return_code=3}} if errors occur during processing.

*Use cases*:

* --igelsession is the name of the storefront session, which only closes storefront sessions, but you cannot specify this option for browser sessions as there is no predefined name for them. if you are running multiple storefront sessions at the same time, and tries to close only one session with this option, it closes all the running storefront session due to Citrix’s limitations.
* --resource option can be used for all session types, resource is the name of the running application, you can specify the resource name between single quotes as it passes the exact string (do not use double quotes because it escapes special characters). If the given name found in the active resources, it terminates that resource. You can pass list of resources at a time separting with ','.
* “--igelsession <SESSION NAME>“ and “--resource <RESOURCE NAME or LIST>“
** When both options are given at the same time, it must perform action to the resource belongs to that particular session name.
*** i.e: five different igelsessions are up and running, all providing a running Calculator app, close only that Calculator that lives under the specified igelsession.
** If the given criteira doesn’t match with the running sessions, it must not perform any action. (return_code=2)

Test with the lasted UMS stable version and note the version

The test case contains all necessary tests to fulfill the status "Hardware continuously verified through IGEL" and to ensure the functionality of the hardware.
Please see also the confluence article about fiber network testing: [https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QA/pages/709918743/Fiber+Network+Testing|https://igel-jira.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/QA/pages/709918743/Fiber+Network+Testing|smart-link] 

*Info to test procedure:*

For this test we use two different thin clients with fiber connection to the fibre switch (static IP addresses)
* H860 with SFP (850nm / 1310 nm)   IP: 192.168.120.209 
* t755 with external fiber card  (LC interface)            IP: 192.168.120.211   (second interface)

* t755 (or as an alternative t660) with external fiber card (SC interface)   IP: 192.168.120.211   (second interface)

Both t755 have a NIC from HP inserted, which needs to be tested at least with every major release.

* First of all install the OS on both devices.
* Setup the LAN connections in tcsetup. On the t755 the external fiber card is the second LAN-Interface.

*-please test 4 different SFP-modules from Huawei and FINISAR with 850 nm and 1310 nm wavelength (4 measurements) -* change the SFP on t755 and/or H860

* always change both SFPs (on switch and device)
* fibre patch cable is always a 5m Mulitmode cable which is needed to protect the laser diodes in the 1310nm SFPs (lower signal level because 1310nm normally uses single mode cable)
* be careful when removing/inserting the SFPs and always protect unused SFPs with the rubber tips (to preserve laser diodes from collecting dust)

* we use iperf3 for connection test. Start the server component in a console with root rights on H860:  iperf3 -s    
* start the iperf3-test on t755:  *iperf3 -c 192.168.120.209 -n 5G*     and   *iperf3 -c 192.168.120.209 -n 5G* *-R*    (for the downstream-test)    
   => at the bottom lines you see the average bandwidth, which must be > 850 MBit/s ; see attached screenshot.

|Parameter|{{Activate post session command}}|
|Registry|{{app.cwa.postsession.enabled}}|
|Type|bool|

|Parameter|{{Execute the command}}|
|Registry|{{app.cwa.postsession.command}}|
|Type|editable|
|Value|_Logoff_ (default) / Shutdown|

If the PSC is then executed, the entered command or program should be executed.

column1: QA | Test Case | Citrix composite USB redirection
column31:
Citrix Workspace app allows the splitting of composite USB devices. A composite USB device can perform more than one function. These functions are accomplished by exposing each of those functions using different interfaces. An example of a composite USB device is the Bloomberg keyboard which consists of a keyboard, fingerprint reader, an audio device, and USB hub, etc.

The Composite USB redirection feature adds the CONNECT value to the rules for USB devices.

CONNECT – Set the “CONNECT” keyword to enable auto-redirect of a device when a session starts.

ALLOW – Set the “ALLOW” keyword to allow auto-redirect of a device only after a session starts. However, if the “CONNECT” or “ALLOW” keyword is set, the device is auto-redirected when it is unplugged and plugged in during a session.

When we redirect the composite USB device, normally the whole device is forwarded to the virtual host. However, now there is the possibility to split and forward only the child interfaces that use a generic USB channel. To do this, we need to add the following filter parameters (split and intf) to the device rules. The split parameter specifies whether a composite device must be forwarded as separate devices or as a single composite device. "Split=1" means that the selected child interfaces of a composite device must be forwarded as split devices, while split=0 must not be forwarded (If the split parameter is omitted, Split=0 is assumed). The if parameter selects the specific child interfaces of the composite unit to which the action is to be applied. 

Find more information here: [https://help-docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-workspace-app/windows/composite-usb-device-redirection.html]

Example:
CONNECT: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=03 # Allow HID device and connect automatically.
DENY: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=00 # Deny audio endpoints
ALLOW: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=05 # Allow mgmt intf but do not connect automatically

column1: QA | Test Case | Citrix composite USB redirection
column31:
Citrix Workspace app allows the splitting of composite USB devices. A composite USB device can perform more than one function. These functions are accomplished by exposing each of those functions using different interfaces. An example of a composite USB device is the Bloomberg keyboard which consists of a keyboard, fingerprint reader, an audio device, and USB hub, etc.

The Composite USB redirection feature adds the CONNECT value to the rules for USB devices.

CONNECT – Set the “CONNECT” keyword to enable auto-redirect of a device when a session starts.

ALLOW – Set the “ALLOW” keyword to allow auto-redirect of a device only after a session starts. However, if the “CONNECT” or “ALLOW” keyword is set, the device is auto-redirected when it is unplugged and plugged in during a session.

When we redirect the composite USB device, normally the whole device is forwarded to the virtual host. However, now there is the possibility to split and forward only the child interfaces that use a generic USB channel. To do this, we need to add the following filter parameters (split and intf) to the device rules. The split parameter specifies whether a composite device must be forwarded as separate devices or as a single composite device. "Split=1" means that the selected child interfaces of a composite device must be forwarded as split devices, while split=0 must not be forwarded (If the split parameter is omitted, Split=0 is assumed). The if parameter selects the specific child interfaces of the composite unit to which the action is to be applied. 

Find more information here: [https://help-docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-workspace-app/windows/composite-usb-device-redirection.html]

Example:
CONNECT: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=03 # Allow HID device and connect automatically.
DENY: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=00 # Deny audio endpoints
ALLOW: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=05 # Allow mgmt intf but do not connect automatically

Citrix Workspace app allows the splitting of composite USB devices. A composite USB device can perform more than one function. These functions are accomplished by exposing each of those functions using different interfaces. An example of a composite USB device is the Bloomberg keyboard which consists of a keyboard, fingerprint reader, an audio device, and USB hub, etc.

The Composite USB redirection feature adds the CONNECT value to the rules for USB devices.

CONNECT – Set the “CONNECT” keyword to enable auto-redirect of a device when a session starts.

ALLOW – Set the “ALLOW” keyword to allow auto-redirect of a device only after a session starts. However, if the “CONNECT” or “ALLOW” keyword is set, the device is auto-redirected when it is unplugged and plugged in during a session.

When we redirect the composite USB device, normally the whole device is forwarded to the virtual host. However, now there is the possibility to split and forward only the child interfaces that use a generic USB channel. To do this, we need to add the following filter parameters (split and intf) to the device rules. The split parameter specifies whether a composite device must be forwarded as separate devices or as a single composite device. "Split=1" means that the selected child interfaces of a composite device must be forwarded as split devices, while split=0 must not be forwarded (If the split parameter is omitted, Split=0 is assumed). The if parameter selects the specific child interfaces of the composite unit to which the action is to be applied. 

Find more information here: [https://help-docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-workspace-app/windows/composite-usb-device-redirection.html]

Example:
CONNECT: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=03 # Allow HID device and connect automatically.
DENY: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=00 # Deny audio endpoints
ALLOW: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=05 # Allow mgmt intf but do not connect automatically

column1: Stabilization of the update process to handle interruptions (network and power)
column31:
See https://jira.igel.com/browse/GPB-981

 

We have customers where the update failed before the usr partition was updated and they now have a unusable system. There are more then one issue here:
 * Boot is not possible as a library is missing which is used by systemd init.
 * WFSD is not working due to other missing libraries
 * also further modules where not on the sys partition which are needed to get a X running
 * igfmount is not handling the usr partition at all as this is done poorly in the initramfs which leads to serious problems:
 ** if the usr partition is missing no update of it will be triggered
 ** if the usr partition parthash do not match the needed one the partition is not deleted or updated
 * The update tools are from a branch which is not clear if it is correct and is maybe missing some fixes.

So serious rework of the update function is needed here.

 

Acceptance Criteria:

Device should still be usable, if an update fails if the network is interrupted and/or the power fails.

Should work with script which make usr partition invalid.

 

Following script was used to make the usr partition invalid so it was not available on the next boot. Not nice but working:
{noformat}
#!/bin/bash -e

temp="$(create_directory -t \
	| sed -n "s#^partition 2:[ \t]*\([0-9]\{1,\}\)-.*#\1# p" \
	| head -n 1)"

if [ "$temp" != "" ]; then
	dd if=/dev/zero of=/dev/igfdisk bs=256k count=1 seek=$temp oflag=direct
	reboot -f
fi{noformat}

*Testprocedure (Check for correct image creation/deployment)*

-on LG device under test: boot with any UDP (UDPocket) and zero out at least the first 3 GB of data on the storage
-Create an OSC Stick and boot it on the LG device
-in the OSC installation switch on the "Factory Image" and insert the factoryID N07R8WC1 (any valid factory ID is o.k. for this test)
-switch on "Automatically shutdown at first boot" 
-Install firmware
-finish installation with shutdown

-plug in an UDP
-as next step make sure that you boot into UDP and NOT the internal storage!
-execute command:  cat /proc/partitions to find out the storage device-name (e.g. mmcblk0, nvme0n1, etc.) 
-execute command:  bootreg dump /dev/<device-name>p4
-check the output for "invalid" for boot_id
-make dd-image of the storage media (store it for example in upload-directory) 
-shutdown UDP and remove UDP

-boot device from internal storage
-check during boot for "Initial Preparations ... please wait" and a green screen with some information written (shown only for 1-2 sec)
-system will perform a shutdown if everything is o.k. 
-boot device from internal storage and perform setup assistant till you are asked for local password
-press CTRL+ALT+F11 for open a rescue console and execute command: bootreg dump /dev/<device-name>p4
-check the output for: installation date: starts with 00000000
-press CTRL+ALT+F1 to switch back to setup assistant and select starter license
-system reboots
-execute command:  bootreg dump /dev/<device-name>p4
 -check the output for: an unique boot_id and installation date: starts with current date
-mount partition p1 to check the log-file check.log:  
   -execute commands:

Steps to perform the update:
 * check with command 'fwupdmgr get-devices' which firmware version is currently installed and what is an appropriate next version (for update/downgrade)
 * Download two suitable cab-files ( for HP Dock G5: [https://fwupd.org/lvfs/devices/com.hp.Dock_USBC_G5.ccgx.dmc.firmware]) to test up- and downgrade (e.g. cab-files V1.0.15.1 und V1.0.14.1)

 * parameter for the cab-filename needs to be set in the registry:  system > registry > update.devices.hp_g5_dock.path ;
also set parameter allow_downgrade  for downgrade-tests
 * trigger firmware update: UMS context menu > Specific Device Command > Update the firmware of an attached G5 Dock
 * check journal during firmware update:  Update/downgrade-file will be transfered to G5 Dock.  At 75% the G5 Dock will be rebooted
 * wait for some minutes until Dock G5 will be recognized by the endpoint again
 * now execute command: 'fwupdmgr get-devices'  to see if the correct version is shown
 * if it shows still the "old" version, please perform a reboot on the endpoint
 * then execute again command: 'fwupdmgr get-devices'  -> now the correct version should be shown

Citrix Workspace app allows the splitting of composite USB devices. A composite USB device can perform more than one function. These functions are accomplished by exposing each of those functions using different interfaces. An example of a composite USB device is the Bloomberg keyboard which consists of a keyboard, fingerprint reader, an audio device, and USB hub, etc.

The Composite USB redirection feature adds the CONNECT value to the rules for USB devices.

CONNECT – Set the “CONNECT” keyword to enable auto-redirect of a device when a session starts.

ALLOW – Set the “ALLOW” keyword to allow auto-redirect of a device only after a session starts. However, if the “CONNECT” or “ALLOW” keyword is set, the device is auto-redirected when it is unplugged and plugged in during a session.

When we redirect the composite USB device, normally the whole device is forwarded to the virtual host. However, now there is the possibility to split and forward only the child interfaces that use a generic USB channel. To do this, we need to add the following filter parameters (split and intf) to the device rules. The split parameter specifies whether a composite device must be forwarded as separate devices or as a single composite device. "Split=1" means that the selected child interfaces of a composite device must be forwarded as split devices, while split=0 must not be forwarded (If the split parameter is omitted, Split=0 is assumed). The if parameter selects the specific child interfaces of the composite unit to which the action is to be applied. 

Find more information here: [https://help-docs.citrix.com/en-us/citrix-workspace-app/windows/composite-usb-device-redirection.html]

Example:
CONNECT: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=03 # Allow HID device and connect automatically.
DENY: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=00 # Deny audio endpoints
ALLOW: vid=047F pid=C039 split=1 intf=05 # Allow mgmt intf but do not connect automatically

column31: Run a Citrix Session via Proxy

The test case contains all necessary tests to fulfill the status "Hardware continuously verified through IGEL" and to ensure the functionality of the hardware.

*Info to test procedure:*

-!! Please do {color:#ce181e}*NO NEW INSTALLATION*{color} of IGEL OS on H860 with fiber optics small form factor pluggable (SFP); all the special settings for this test environment would be lost (Stefan Gottwald could set it up again); only do an update/upgrade to the desired IGEL OS version

-The Device under Test (UD7 H860) is connected to a Router/Fileserver (which is a UD6 H830 next to the H860. On the H830 a special linux system (Zentyal) is running. User: elch  PW: h********3

It provides a file server for the /smbmount (which is the mount point for //192.168.120.1/qs) The router is connected to PROD-Network and to the Switch (for the fibre tests to H860).

*-Please test 4 different SFP-modules from Huawei and FINISAR with 850 nm and 1310 nm wavelength (4 measurements)*

  * always change both SFPs (on switch and H860)
   * fibre patch cable is always a 5m Mulitmode cable which is needed to protect the laser diodes in the 1310nm SFPs (lower signal level because 1310nm normally uses single mode cable)
   * be careful when removing/inserting the SFPs and always protect unused SFPs with the rubber tips (to preserve laser diodes from collecting dust)
   * start the server component on the H830/Zentyal in a console with root rights:  iperf3 -s    
   * start the test on H860:  iperf3 -c 192.168.120.1 -n 5G    
     * this transfers 5GB data and shows a table with statistics; at the bottom lines you see the average bandwidth, which must be > 850 MBit/s ; see attached screenshot

 

-For logging in to the H860 from your workplace:  ssh root@172.30.91.109  -p 2210  (port forwarding from H830 to H860, IP is dynamic)

 -In case of a lost smb mount, just perform a reboot

IGEL delivers a self-expanding Preload Factory Image to HP that can be installed regardless of the module size. 

The endpoint must not be initially booted before it leaves the factory. 

The first boot process takes place at the customer's site. 

If it is necessary to boot the endpoint for testing, it must be reloaded with the Preload Factory Image provided by IGEL. 

As part of the final tests, it is assumed that a CRC check of the Preload Factory Image has been performed. 

At least two endpoints are required for successful testing.

 

See document for further information for what to test.

column31:
Added Wi-Fi/LAN automatic switch feature. This feature can be enabled using "network.applet.wireless.enable_wifi_auto_switch" registry key. By enabling this key, a submenu will be added to Wi-Fi manager applet which gives the user the ability to select Wi-Fi operation among on, off and automatic modes. column1: LXOS 11.06.100 | New Feature | post session commands multi-protocol
column31: Multi-session support. Under 'System > Firmware Customization > Custom Commands > Post Session', users are now able to define multiple Session types which will all be covered by the post-session command mechanism. If multiple sessions are running simultaneously, only when the last running session exits (successfully), the post-session command executes. https://jira.igel.com/browse/LX7-3610

New implementation because there were some drawbacks regarding reliability with the former post-session command architecture. (Drop-in replacement, so no changes from an enduser perspective like triggering logic or settings) https://jira.igel.com/browse/LX7-4574

The test case contains all the necessary basic tests to verify that the Custom Parition works without errors and can be rolled out.

*Important:* To test the Boot options you have to press and *hold* the keys until the system boots. The reason for that is, that the time slot of the system for detecting the wanted boot option is very short and could else be missed.

The test case contains all necessary tests to fulfill the status "Hardware continuously verified through IGEL" and to ensure the functionality of the hardware.

Info to test procedure:

-The Device under Test (UD7 H860) is connected to a Router/Fileserver (which is a UD6 H830 next to the H860. On the H830 a special linux system (Zentyal) is running. User: elch  PW: h********3

It provides a file server for the /smbmount (which is the mount point for //192.168.120.1/qs.  The router is connected to PROD-Network and to the Switch (for the fibre tests to H860).

-For testing the file transfer:  
   * On the H860 open a terminal and change directory to  /smbmount/QA/IGEL Referenzvideos
   * command:  dd if=t4k.mp4  of=/dev/null bs=1M status=progress   (this should show a transfer rate of about 65 MB/s)

 

-For testing the different GBIC modules from Huawei and FINISAR with 850 nm and 1310 nm wavelength  on  a low OSI level:
   * 4 measurements are needed, always change both GBICs (on switch and H860)
   * fibre patch cable is always a 5m Mulitmode cable which is needed to protect the laser diodes in the 1300nm GBICs (lower signal level because 1300nm normally uses single mode cable)
   * be careful when removing/inserting the GBICs and always protect unused GBICs with the rubber tips (to preserve laser diodes from collecting dust)
   * start the server component on the H830/Zentyal in a console with root rights:  iperf3 -s    
   * start the test on H860:  iperf3 -c 192.168.120.1 -n 5G    
     * this transfers 5GB data and shows a table with statistics; at the bottom lines you see the average bandwidth, which must be > 850 MBit/s ; see attached screenshot

 
 -Additional tests:  
   * play a video with media player via /smbmount and check for smooth play back
   * perform an Igel OS update  and an IGEL OS upgrade (to new rc level)

 
 -For logging in to the H860 from your workplace:  ssh root@172.30.91.109  -p 2210  (port forwarding from H830 to H860)

 -In case of a lost smb mount, just perform a reboot

h2. General

With 10.05.800 and upwards it is possible to upgrade an OS installation to mainline version 11. However, there are some restrictions about the underlying hardware:
 * CPU supports 64-bit mode
 * At least 2GB RAM
 * At least 2GB flash memory
 * *No VIA graphics*
 * Device has no configured special network (PPTP, OpenVPN, NCP, CAG VPN, Genucard, LTE)
 * Device is supported (see below)
 * Device is not unsupported or discontinued (see below)

See [Devices Supported by OSC and UD Pocket|https://kb.igel.com/igelos-11.01.100/en/devices-supported-by-osc-and-ud-pocket-10327369.html]

h2. Additional information

The following prerequisites are checked one after the other:

+Hardware:+
 * Supported hardware
 * RAM
 * Flash size
 * VIA graphics

 

+License:+
 * Only OS 11 license will be checked (Workspace Edition).
 * A registry key ({{update.migrate_to_11_enterprise_required}}) defines whether a EMP is retrieved.  There are three values: on, off, smart (default). Value smart checks whether a feature is used that requires EMP (e.g. SWP, ICG).

 

+Setup:+
 * Allow migration (registry key: {{update.firmware_migrate_to_11}})
 * If migration fails, a registry key is available to overwrite (registry key: {{update.force_firmware_migrate_to_11}})
 * If PowerTerm is configured, a registry key is available to overwrite (registry key: {{update.migrate_to_11_with_powerterm}})
 * Custom Partition (is always deleted, even if EMP is available)
 * Valid Update source
 * Valid Network settings
 * Battery state is not allowed (OS only)

 

Once the upgrade has been confirmed, the following processes occur:
 * Restart is triggered
 * Upgrade is started automatically
 * Restart is triggered
 * OS 11 should boot

 

+Warning:+

As soon as the upgrade indicator has a red background, the device is in a critical state. Here an AC loss would lead to an unstable system - probably even broken.

On the client side, a job is run periodically that checks if the current battery level differs from the last reported level by a certain percentage. This percentage can be configured in the registry at {{system.remotemanager.battery_report_frequency}}. The following frequencies can be configured:

* Often    (3%)
* Normal  (7%)
* Rarely   (11%)
* Very Rarely  (17%)
* Never

The periodic job stores the battery level in the file {{/var/state/battery_level}}. If the last stored level differs by the above configured percentage, the script {{/config/bin/collect_battery_level}} stores the new value and calls the rmagent function {{write_runtime_information}} which reports the new level to UMS.

See http://jira.igel.local/browse/LX6-921 and http://jira.igel.local/browse/UMS-5548 for further information.

column31: For a description of Kerberos on Linux Thin Clients see https://ssl.igel.de/intranet/knowledge-base/howtos/linux-firmware/single-sign-on-with-kerberos-on-igel-linux-thin-clients

Kerberos is an authentication service. It operates with entities of users, services and computers which are called _principals_. These principals all belong to a _realm_, an administrative unit. Each principal has a unique _principal name_ inside the realm. To provide the authentication system a service called _key distribution center_ is used.

As an example Microsoft Windows Domains build a realm. The Windows Domain name is the realm name (in upper case letters), e.g. @EXAMPLE.COM@. A user principal would be e.g. @user@EXAMPLE.COM@. The domain controllers take the role of the key distribution centers.

When logging in, a user gets a _ticket granting ticket_ from the key distribution center. This ticket expires after a certain time (usually 1 day). When the user e.g. starts an ICA session, the client can get a so called _service ticket_ from the key distribution center with the aid of the ticket granting ticket. With this service ticket the authentication at the ICA server is accomplished.

column31:
Our terminals could be configured with different color depths (16 ("Thousands") and 24 bit (Millions)).  They have to be supported by rdesktop and RemoteFX.

As soon as a VM is using true RemoteFX, the used color depth is always the highest as possible (e.g. in our case 24bit).
References (many hits in Google):
https://wtware.com/docs5/remotefx.html
https://www.cybelesoft.com/helps/thinfinity/remote-desktop/workstation/index.html?remotefx.html

So, after changing the colour depth to e.g. 16bit, nevertheless 24bit or 32bit are used within the RDP session.

Use this site within session for checking the currently configured colour depth:
http://browser-information.online-domain-tools.com/
(Java required. If this URL should not be vaild one day anymore, google for another one).

ICA USB Redirection makes USB devices plugged into a thin client available in a ICA
XenDesktop session. Note: Isochronous features in USB devices are not supported (= Headsets, Webcams)!
Which USB devices should be remoted is controled by USB policy. There are three types of policy rules:
1. Class rule: based on ClassID/SubclassID/ProtocolID device's definition
2. Device rule: based on VendorID/ProductID/ReleaseID device's definition
3. Default rule: applied if neither class rule nor device rule was triggered.
The default value of default policy rule is "DENY". 
To test the ICA USB redirection, using of a USB printer or USB scanner is recommended.

column31:
Test with all Citrix Session Types

ICA USB Redirection makes USB devices plugged into a thin client available in a ICA
XenDesktop session. Note: Isochronous features in USB devices are not supported (= Headsets, Webcams)!
Which USB devices should be remoted is controled by USB policy. There are three types of policy rules:
1. Class rule: based on ClassID/SubclassID/ProtocolID device's definition
2. Device rule: based on VendorID/ProductID/ReleaseID device's definition
3. Default rule: applied if neither class rule nor device rule was triggered.
The default value of default policy rule is "DENY". 
To test the ICA USB redirection, using of a USB printer or USB scanner is recommended.
